newsitem.title: UK: LASMO doubles profits, sees rosy future.
newsitem.headline: LASMO doubles profits, sees rosy future.

text.p: British oil exploration company LASMO Plc posted a near doubling in its 1996 profits on Thursday to 67 million pounds ($109 million), and chief executive Joe Darby painted a rosy picture of LASMO's oil production prospects.

"While clearly aided by the unexpected strength of world oil prices, the improvement also reflects the quality of our underlying asssets and the tight control of costs," said Darby. Average oil prices per barrel rose to $18.72 in 1996 from $17.09.

Darby said initial results from LASMO's current appraisal activity indicate that reserve additions in 1997 are likely to more than replace production. Appraisal and development activity will enable the company to reach its target of 200,000 barrels of oil per day by the end of this year and to sustain this level beyond 2000.
Peak production from Indonesia and initial contributions from its new British oil fields led to the highest ever level of production for the company in 1996.
The company said its 1997 exploration programme will be focused on its ley regions of Britain, Indonesia, North Africa, Italy and Pakistan.

In Algeria a successful appraisal programme enabled more reserves to be booked and the first phase of development started in the year. The company increased its dividend to 2.0p per share and said it now has more financial capacity to invest with gearing down to 27 percent from 37 percent.
